notes.text: Parker Wotherspoon is on injured reserve and has missed the last 10 games. Jérémy Lauzon has taken his spot beside Rasmus Andersson. That pair has had 37% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 106:20 together, down from 54% with Wotherspoon.

Victor Olofsson is on injured reserve and has missed the last 12 games. Raphaël Lavoie has taken his spot beside Tomáš Hertl and Trevor Connelly. That line has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 65:02 together.
Jonas Røndbjerg was added to the roster on Oct 31 and has played beside Nic Dowd and Marc Gatcomb.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 10th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 69% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 54:40 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.
Kaedan Korczak is day to day (lower body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their more valuable skaters.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.
Evgeni Malkin is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Ilya Solovyov was added to the roster on Oct 20 and has played beside Kris Letang.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Golden Knights won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in Vegas on Oct 17. The Golden Knights (9-5-2) lost 3-2 in a shootout to Boston last night, and the Penguins (5-7-2) lost 5-4 to Montréal on Saturday. Going in, the Golden Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for fifth in the NHL) and the Pens sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 26th).

The Golden Knights have played better than their record (.625) says: their chances are worth about .681, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Penguins (.429 on chances worth .558), mostly because they’re 3-5 in one-goal games.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st), but have had shaky goaltending (31st). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), so the Penguins’ struggling power play gets a tough test from their penalty killers. The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Penguins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Golden Knights.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 16 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring, and Mark Stone (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 16 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. The Penguins’ scoring runs through Erik Karlsson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 14 GP), who has seven points in his last five games. Nick Robertson (6 G / 0 A / 6 P in 14 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Adin Hill (5-2-0 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to start for Vegas, and Artūrs Šilovs (5-3-1 / .889 SV% in 9 GS) for Pittsburgh.
At home, Dan Muse likes to send Dewar, Lizotte and Robertson out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Barbashev, Eichel and Stone.

items.text: The Golden Knights have been without Parker Wotherspoon and Victor Olofsson for several games.

The Penguins are newly without Elmer Söderblom and Evgeni Malkin, and have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk since Oct 9. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
Mark Stone has nine goals on chances worth about 5.4 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Kaedan Korczak is a game-time decision, NHL.com says.
